paragraphs: A Salmonella outbreak linked to broccoli sprouts is now over, the CDC reported this week [1]. The outbreak caused 34 illnesses across six states with three hospitalizations and no deaths [1]. The sprouts were grown from a contaminated seed lot imported from New Zealand, though authorities did not name the seed supplier [16].

The USDA issued a public health alert for Betterballen Foods LLC "Bami Rolls" sold in Georgia and South Carolina due to undeclared sesame allergen [2][9]. Consumers with these products should not eat them if they have a sesame allergy [9].

Brad's Raw Chips is recalling certain Brad's Crunchy Kale & Veggie Chips products because they may contain thallium [4]. The FDA also updated its list of cinnamon products with dangerously high lead levels, adding Wise Wife brand ground cinnamon from SLR Food Distribution Inc. to bring the total to 21 affected products [19].
